findings.text: The mutation classifier tokenises with re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+'), which does not match the underscore, so any identifier carrying a _set / set_ / _merge / _create / _delete / _remove / _drop segment yields a token equal to a mutation keyword and a READ-ONLY statement is suppressed - returning [] silently rather than refusing. TRIGGERING INPUT, and it is already in the tree: imas_codex/standard_names/protection.py:100, the read-only query inside automatic_deletion_protections. It contains no mutating clause; it projects sn.catalog_merge_commit_sha, which splits to CATALOG / MERGE / COMMIT / SHA, and _cypher_mutation_clause returns 'MERGE'. I ran the node's own classifier over all 771 cypher-like triple-quoted statements in imas_codex/standard_names, comparing its verdict against a bare-word oracle on the same literal-stripped text, and this is the one live disagreement. Consequence if the guard ever covers that call: a protection check returns the empty set, which reads as 'no durable authority bars deletion' - the permissive answer, produced silently. MITIGATION TODAY: automatic_deletion_protections is reached from the derived-parent cleanup in graph_ops (3483) and from protection.py's own callers, not from sn_review, so no statement on the report-only review path is currently misclassified. VERDICT: SHOULD-FIX, not MUST-FIX - the fix is one character class, tokenising on r'[A-Za-z_]+' and comparing the whole token, which makes catalog_merge_commit_sha a single non-matching token. The node's suite cannot see this because every statement it classifies is synthesised in the test file.

_WriteSuppressingRun.run returns a bare list for a suppressed statement, so the no-op is not Result-shaped: a suppressed write whose receipt is consumed raises AttributeError instead of being silently dropped. REPRODUCED, not argued - with a driver stub whose run() returns an object exposing consume() and single(), inside _suppress_review_graph_writes: session.run("MERGE (n:X {id:1})").consume() gives "AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'consume'", and session.run('MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n RETURN count(n) as count').single() gives "AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'single'". Two in-tree sites would hit it: imas_codex/standard_names/dd_resolutions.py:706 calls transaction.run(_GRAPH_PORT_WRITE_QUERY, records=new_records).consume(), and imas_codex/graph/client.py:509 calls result.single() on 'MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n RETURN count(n) as count' inside clear_database. Neither is on the sn review path, so report-only does not crash today; GraphClient.query, which is what the review writers use, only iterates its result and so tolerates []. VERDICT: SHOULD-FIX. A tiny stub exposing single() -> None, data() -> [], consume() -> None and __iter__ over an empty sequence makes the suppression a true no-op for every caller shape rather than for the iterating ones only.

9 of the 22 parametrised cases assert 0 == 0, and one of them is the method that matters most. I ran the test module's own helpers outside pytest: of 22 enumerated methods, 13 deliver at least one mutating statement to the recorder unguarded (79 statements in total) and 9 deliver none - compare_facilities, find_shared_imas_mappings, get_facilities, get_facility, get_label_counts, get_nodes_across_facilities, get_nodes_by_facility, get_stats and QUERY. For those 9 the control half is empty, so 'assert _mutations(guarded_session) == []' and 'assert len(suppressed) == len(would_write)' are both satisfied by an instrument that never looked. The 'query' case is the notable one, because _SAMPLE_ARGUMENTS['cypher'] is the read-only 'MATCH (n) RETURN n' while gc.query is exactly the route the production review writers (write_name_review_results / write_docs_review_results) use for their UNWIND ... SET. The property is not unguarded - test_review_path_writes_of_each_shape_are_refused drives query with a real MERGE and asserts the receipt reads ['MERGE','MERGE','MERGE'] - so this is an aperture note, not a defect. Changing _SAMPLE_ARGUMENTS['cypher'] to a mutating statement would convert the 'query' case from vacuous to load-bearing in one line, and the parametrised test already carries the control half needed to prove it. VERDICT: NIT with a one-line fix.

justifications.durability: The chosen shape is the durable one and it is the right call: a guard on the boundary covers a method added to GraphClient tomorrow without anyone remembering to name it, which is exactly the failure a per-method list has. The docstring says so in mechanism terms. Two residuals keep this at 14, both in the guard's DECISION FUNCTION rather than its aperture, both invisible to the node's suite, and both with a silent failure mode. FIRST, _cypher_mutation_clause tokenises with re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+') over the upper-cased statement, and that pattern does not match the underscore - so any identifier containing a _set / set_ / _merge / _create / _delete / _remove / _drop segment splits into a token that equals a mutation keyword, and a READ-ONLY statement is classified as a mutation and silently returns []. This is not hypothetical: I ran the node's own classifier over all 771 cypher-like statements in imas_codex/standard_names and it misclassifies a live one, imas_codex/standard_names/protection.py:100 - the read-only deletion-protection query, flagged MERGE purely because it projects sn.catalog_merge_commit_sha. Under the guard that query returns no rows, which is the PERMISSIVE answer from a protection check. It is off the sn review path today (automatic_deletion_protections is reached from the derived-parent cleanup in graph_ops, not from sn_review), so nothing is broken now - which is precisely why it is a durability finding and not a MUST-FIX: it is a guard whose classifier is already wrong on real repository Cypher, one identifier away from being wrong on the review path, and nothing in the delivered suite would say so. SECOND, the suppressed return value is a bare list, not a Result-shaped stub, so a suppressed write whose receipt is consumed raises instead of no-opping. Two in-tree sites would: imas_codex/standard_names/dd_resolutions.py:706 does transaction.run(_GRAPH_PORT_WRITE_QUERY, ...).consume(), and imas_codex/graph/client.py:509 does result.single() on a DETACH DELETE ... RETURN count(n). Both are off the review path, and both are demonstrated below. The good news on the other side of the ledger, which I checked because a false NEGATIVE would be far worse than a false positive: the repository uses no apoc, no CALL db.index...create*, and no setNodeVectorProperty, so there is currently no procedure-style or string-carried mutation that the keyword scan would miss. The scan direction that matters is safe today.
justifications.evidence: Strong, and the parts I could independently reproduce, I did. The focused gate: I re-ran tests/standard_names/test_review_write_suppression.py myself at the committed head e713336fc, from the worker's worktree against the shared .venv with PYTHONPATH set to that worktree, and got 25 passed, 1 warning in 27.14s, EXIT=0 (log at the reviewer-gate.log path in my run directory) - the manifest's '25 passed in 15.90s' is the same result. The negative control is the right mutation and its log is a real red log: the first line reads 'negative_control: replace the session-boundary write suppression in _suppress_review_graph_writes with a GraphClient.query-only guard (the aperture the predecessor shipped)', which names the recorded defect verbatim, and the run is 15 failed, 10 passed, 1 warning in 17.89s. The failing set is exactly right for that mutation: the parametrised cases that go red are the methods that reach the driver through create_node, create_relationship or a direct session block - ensure_vector_indexes, ensure_fulltext_indexes, initialize_schema among them - plus test_review_path_writes_of_each_shape_are_refused, while the read helpers stay green. That is the query-only aperture failing on precisely the methods it cannot see, which is the defect this node repairs, shown failing before the repair. Both commits are clean on the trailer check (0 hits for co-authored-by / generated with / claude / copilot) and both carry substantive bodies. Two honest gaps, both declared rather than papered over. First, there is no baseline/after suite pair; the manifest's reason is correct and checkable - base fe5012a13 does not contain the predecessor's suppression at all, so there is no prior revision of this guard to measure against and the negative control IS the pre-repair snapshot. Second, and this is the reason for 18 rather than 20: the node's evidence measures the guard against SYNTHESISED statements from a recording driver, never against the statements the review path actually issues. That aperture is what let both findings below survive its gate - I found each by running the node's own classifier over the repository's real Cypher (771 cypher-like statements in imas_codex/standard_names), which is a measurement the node could have made and did not.
justifications.fit: Idiomatic for this repository. The contextmanager guard restores GraphClient.session in a finally block, the two proxies share their run() through a small base class so the session and transaction paths cannot drift, and the docstrings state the MECHANISM and the concrete alternative they reject ('a narrower aperture silently writes through') rather than narrating a changelog or citing a plan. The new CLI flag is guarded by explicit click.UsageError checks against --dry-run and --skip-audit, which is the right shape for two flags whose combination has no meaning. The closure is subtle but correct: `with _suppress_review_graph_writes() as suppressed_graph_writes` rebinds the same local cell that the nested _run reads, so the receipt line prints the guard's own count and not the empty placeholder - I traced this rather than assuming it. Naming and comment hygiene are clean. One fit cost holds this at 17: 9 of the 22 parametrised cases in test_no_write_capable_method_reaches_the_graph are vacuous, because the method delivers no mutation unguarded so both sides of the comparison are zero - compare_facilities, find_shared_imas_mappings, get_facilities, get_facility, get_label_counts, get_nodes_across_facilities, get_nodes_by_facility, get_stats and, most notably, QUERY, whose _SAMPLE_ARGUMENTS entry is the read-only 'MATCH (n) RETURN n'. The test's own docstring acknowledges the zero-on-both-sides case, and test_review_path_writes_of_each_shape_are_refused covers query with a real MERGE, so the property is not unguarded - but 9 of 25 green cases assert 0 == 0, and the parametrised case named 'query' reads as coverage of the single most important method while exercising nothing. A mutating cypher sample would fix it in one line.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The brief was to make the report-only write suppression cover every write-capable GraphClient method, with a test that enumerates them by introspection. Delivered exactly, and I verified the load-bearing premise rather than reading it off the manifest. The premise is that GraphClient.session is the SOLE route from the client to a Neo4j session: I grepped every self._driver reference in imas_codex/graph/client.py and the only two self._driver.session() calls are at 284 and 287, both INSIDE session() itself (the second is the reconnect retry); every one of the 20 remaining graph-touching bodies opens `with self.session() as sess` (367, 422, 478, 507, 518, 535, 558, 636, 692, 711, 805, 815, 835, 865, 885, 926, 939, 956). So replacing the class attribute GraphClient.session is a complete aperture over the client, which is what the goal asked for and what a per-method guard cannot give. The enumeration is real introspection, not a maintained list: inspect.getmembers(GraphClient, inspect.isfunction) plus a fixed-point closure over `self.<name>(` references, seeded at 'session'. I ran it myself outside pytest and reproduced the manifest's three headline numbers exactly - 22 methods enumerated, 13 of them delivering at least one mutating statement to the recorder unguarded, 79 mutating statements in total across those 13 (_initialize_schema_impl=22, initialize_schema=22, ensure_vector_indexes=17, ensure_fulltext_indexes=5, create_diagnostic=3, create_mdsplus_server=3, create_nodes=1, create_node=1, create_relationship=1, create_facility=1, create_imas_path=1, ensure_facility=1, drop_all=1). Under the guard all 79 are dropped and all 79 are receipted. I also checked the review path's actual writer: persist_review_worker routes through write_name_review_results / write_docs_review_results, which issue their UNWIND ... SET through gc.query, which opens self.session() - so the production write the mode exists to suppress genuinely passes the guarded boundary. The reason this is 19 rather than 20 is the flag surface rather than the aperture: because the dispatch base lacks the predecessor's commit, this node had to introduce --report-only itself as well as widen it, so the goal as landed is slightly larger than the goal as briefed - correctly disclosed in the manifest, but it is the coordinator who now owns a reconciliation.
justifications.scope_discipline: Clean. The whole diff fe5012a13..e713336fc is 4 files, 423 insertions, 2 deletions, and the four files are exactly the four declared write paths: imas_codex/cli/sn.py (+136/-2), tests/standard_names/test_review_write_suppression.py (+230), docs/evidence/archive/sn-catalog-audit-instrument-landed.html (+51), docs/plans/sn-catalog-audit-instrument.html (+8). Nothing belonging to a concurrent node is touched - in particular imas_codex/standard_names/review/enrichment.py and the prompts under imas_codex/llm/prompts/sn/ are untouched, and the predecessor's tests/standard_names/test_review_report_only.py, which is explicitly NOT in this node's scope, is not modified. No existing test is edited, no assertion weakened, no conftest or shared fixture touched. Two commits, both conventional subject plus body, neither pushed nor merged, no branch created, and the node did not resolve its own driving followup. Naming is clean throughout: no plan label, sprint id, stage name, ticket reference or author attribution in filenames, symbols, comments or docstrings; the test file is named for what it guards. The reason this is 18 rather than 20 is not a scope violation but a scope COLLISION the node found and reported rather than caused: because the dispatch base predates the predecessor's commit 3d7f56cc4, this node's imas_codex/cli/sn.py edit and the unmerged predecessor's edit to the same file overlap - both add the --report-only option, the mutual-exclusion checks and the asyncio.run wrapper. The manifest states this first and names the two commits, which is the right handling, but the coordinator must reconcile the two sn.py edits at integration rather than merge both.
